summary: Repaired telemetry-heartbeat.service by correcting only ExecStart. The service now runs the preserved program as svc-heartbeat, refreshes its heartbeat every second, retains all existing hardening, and recovered successfully after one node1 reboot.
actions_performed: Diagnosed systemd status 203/EXEC caused by the nonexistent telemetry-heartbeat-missing path.
Changed ExecStart to /usr/local/bin/telemetry-heartbeat, reloaded systemd, and restarted the service.
Verified runtime identity, heartbeat cadence, file ownership, and effective security restrictions.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified its boot ID changed and the service recovered.

evidence.summary: The installed script remains intact and executable; only ExecStart was corrected to reference it.
Post-restart runtime state shows active/running, User and Group svc-heartbeat, and the correct command.

evidence.requirement: Heartbeat refreshed at least every five seconds
evidence.summary: Six post-restart samples show consecutive one-second timestamp and mtime updates with svc-heartbeat ownership.
The original restrictions and post-restart effective properties match, including strict filesystem protection, no new privileges, empty capability bounding set, and restricted address families.
Healthy baseline boot ID 54bd1c3e-3a1b-4913-841b-88512119e096 was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 01629b4f-2de4-4c17-8467-28c5c2c6e547 observed, and service/data health reconfirmed.
